vopros: I run a small service business in Los Angeles and customers keep haggling on price. Who in LA can help me with that?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Dealing with price haggling is a common challenge, and there are several LA-based resources that can help you build pricing confidence and negotiation skills. Let me find some current options for you.Good news — there are several free, no-cost resources in LA specifically set up to help small business owners with pricing strategy, sales confidence, and handling customer pushback. Here's who to reach out to:

## 1. SCORE Los Angeles (Free)
This is probably your best first stop. SCORE Los Angeles offers free business mentoring in Los Angeles County, including LA, Pasadena, Glendale, and Santa Monica, plus parts of Kern County. Their volunteers are successful real-world business professionals who volunteer thousands of hours to help existing and startup businesses succeed, and they include experts with experience in sales, marketing, and pricing among other business disciplines.

You can specifically search their mentor directory for people with sales/pricing backgrounds — for example, some mentors list "Pricing" and "Product Development" among their areas of expertise. Since it's one-on-one mentoring, you can literally walk through your pricing sheet, your sales pitch, and how you respond when a customer says "can you do it cheaper?"

**Where to go:** score.org/losangeles

## 2. LA Regional Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Network (Free)
This is a federally-backed network with multiple locations across LA County (Pasadena, Long Beach, Santa Clarita/San Fernando Valley, San Gabriel Valley, and more). The Los Angeles Small Business Development Center is a federally-funded resource that provides business owners with no cost one-on-one assistance in business planning, management, marketing, sales, procurement, and strategic planning, as well as access to financing.

Because they have seven SBDC service centers in the LA Regional Network, each hosted at a local organization deeply connected to their respective communities, offering low-cost business training and no-cost one-on-one advising services, you can find one near you and get sales/pricing coaching tailored to your industry (e.g., home services, cleaning, contracting, etc.).

**Where to go:** smallbizla.org

## 3. LA Business Navigator / City of LA
The city itself maintains a portal connecting you to these vetted resources — SCORE LA engages a network of former business owners and executives to provide free business consulting, mentoring and professional guidance to existing and emerging small businesses — accessible through business.lacity.gov.

---

### Practical tip
When you meet with a SCORE or SBDC advisor, ask specifically for help with:
- **Value-based pricing scripts** (how to explain *why* your price is what it is)
- **Anchoring techniques** (presenting a higher-tier option first so your standard price looks reasonable)
- **Handling "can you match a competitor's quote"** conversations without racing to the bottom

Both SCORE and SBDC are completely free (no strings attached, no sales pitch), so it's worth booking sessions with both and seeing which mentor's style clicks for your specific service industry.
